overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the Committee said it no longer relies on the OML for the redactions, so the minutes are not withheld under the OML. Privilege and Public Records questions go to the Supervisor of Records.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Committee kept redacting portions of nine sets of released executive session minutes after the executive session purposes were served.
allegations.key_passage: Because the redacted portions of the executive session minutes are not being withheld from the public under the Open Meeting Law, we find no violation of that law.

allegations.summary: A second allegation about one set of minutes was raised, but the complainant withdrew it in the request for further review.
allegations.key_passage: In his request for further review, the Complainant withdrew the additional allegation.

allegations.summary: Whether the Committee's attorney-client privilege and Public Records Law redaction claims are justified was not decided by the AG.
allegations.key_passage: does not give the Division the authority to determine whether the Committee’s assertion of the attorney-client privilege is justified or whether an exemption to the Public Records Law applies
